says.detail:
Drafted.

I am writing to complain about the care I received at the Emergency Unit, University Hospital of Wales, Heath Park, Cardiff, after I injured my right wrist.

On 2026-09-12, I slipped on wet steps and fell on my outstretched right hand. I attended the Emergency Unit at University Hospital of Wales, where my wrist was X-rayed. I was told it was a sprain and was sent home with a bandage and no follow-up.

The pain did not go away. On 2026-10-19, my GP sent me for a repeat X-ray and MRI.

On 2026-10-26, the MRI showed a displaced scaphoid waist fracture that has not healed, and surgery is now planned.

This has had a significant impact on me. I have missed class tests and weeks of shifts at my café job.

I would also like to ask about the following guidance. The Welsh Government / NICE recommendation says: "Consider MRI for first-line imaging in people with suspected scaphoid fractures following a thorough clinical examination." Please could you explain how this recommendation was followed in my care at my first attendance.

I would like an explanation of what happened, an apology, changes to how A&E checks wrist injuries, and compensation for the pain I have experienced and my lost earnings.

To complain, it says you can fill in the Complaints Form, e-mail the team, write to the address given, or call during office hours; it also says Llais can provide complaints advocacy and support.

To: Cardiff and Vale University Health Board
University Hospital of Wales is part of Cardiff and Vale University Health Board in NHS Wales, so this is a public NHS Wales complaint. The Health Board says to raise concerns with the staff involved first; if that does not resolve it, use its 'Listening to People' complaints process by phone, email, post, or its downloadable complaints form. The newer Welsh Government page says concerns raised after 31 March 2026 follow 'Listening to People', while older pages still refer to 'Putting Things Right'.
